## To Discuss

- Two ways to give a function its parameters. 14 of 25 wrote `f(d)` with R, L, m and rho set inside the function, as in the reference. 10 of 25 passed them in, `f(d, R, L, m, rho)`, and handed `fzero` a one-input wrapper, `@(d) f(d, R, L, m, rho)`. Both are correct. We have not covered the second form yet (anonymous functions come in week 7), so it is worth understanding why it works: `fzero` only ever calls its function with one input.
- Count both hulls. One draft came out at 0.138 m, which is the answer for a single hull: the factor of 2 is missing. When an answer is off by a clean factor, look for a missing count, constant or unit.
- Write the model before the code. 20 of 25 wrote both the equilibrium equation and the rearranged f(d) = 0 in text. The one-hull and missing-length mistakes this week would both have shown up in a written equation.
